prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a retail clothing area, the depth map shows the camera wearer's hand holding a smartphone at bottom-center within arm's reach (about 0.3–0.4 m away, brightest white), a clothing rack with hanging trousers and sweaters immediately to the right at 0.5–1.2 m (within arm's reach of both the wearer and the nearby man), and a man standing to the left at roughly 1.2–1.8 m away, about 0.5–0.8 m left of the rack. In frames 1–4 the camera looks downward so the man's upper body is cropped above the frame while he shifts his stance slightly and faces toward the wearer; in frame 5 the camera pitches up to show the man's torso and head facing and looking toward the wearer at ~1.5 m on the left, while the rack with hangers (~0.6–1.0 m) partially occludes a second person standing further behind it on the right (~2.0–2.5 m) in front of a rear wall and doorway (~3–4 m). The continuous brightness gradients make the sloped floor plane, the layered depth of individual hanging garments on the right rack, and the step in distance between the foreground rack and background doorway clearer than in RGB alone. However, the depth map is unreliable around the thin metal rack legs, where the man's shoes blend into the floor luminance in frames 1–4, and along the upper background wall in frame 1 where depth drops to black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the standing man on the left (`person` mask) at ~1.2–1.8 m from the camera wearer and the wearer's own hands and handheld phone (`person` and `cell phone` masks) at ~0.3–0.4 m in the bottom foreground, within the wearer's arm's reach. Across frames 1–4, only the lower body and legs of the man on the left are visible in the downward view as his feet turn slightly toward the wearer, while the wearer's right thumb partially occludes the phone screen; in frame 5, the camera tilts up to reveal the man's head and torso facing the wearer on the left, a distant background person partly occluded behind him on the far left (~3 m), and a person on the right (~2 m, facing away) partly occluded by the foreground clothing rack (~0.6–1.0 m). Compared to RGB, the masks sharply delineate the boundary between the wearer's fingers and the phone in frame 2 and separate the overlapping people on the far left and far right in frame 5. However, the map is highly unreliable on the clothing racks and accessories: it misses the phone in frames 1, 4, and 5, misclassifies the hanging jeans (~0.8–1.2 m on the right, within arm's reach) as a `person` in frames 2 and 4 and the right-hand sweater rack as a `suitcase` in frame 3, and in frame 5 mislabels the man's lanyard as a `tie` and the foreground hangers and clothes as a `bed` and `person`.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks skeletal keypoints in only two of the five frames, showing the standing man on the left at roughly 1.2–1.8 m from the camera wearer (and ~0.5–0.8 m left of the clothing rack) while leaving the foreground hands, phone (~0.3–0.4 m), and surrounding racks (~0.5–1.2 m, within arm's reach) unmapped on the black background. In frame 1, yellow body keypoints map the man's crossed arms, torso, hips, knees, and ankles on the left—with his head cropped out of view above the top edge—showing his body angled toward the right and facing roughly toward the camera wearer. Across frames 2–4, as the camera remains angled downward and only the man's waist and legs remain in view, all body and hand skeletons disappear completely. In frame 5, after the camera tilts upward, a cluster of yellow facial keypoints and a horizontal shoulder bar appear on the left at ~1.5 m, confirming that the man's shoulders and face are oriented directly toward the camera wearer while his lower body is cropped below the frame. The skeleton in frame 1 clarifies the exact joint positions of his folded arms and hip-to-ankle alignment under loose clothing better than RGB alone, but the map is unreliable because it fails to detect his visible legs in frames 2–4, misses the wearer's foreground hands in all frames, and omits the two partially occluded background people in frame 5.
